title: Small US chocolate maker
subtitle: Dark chocolate bars and boxes, as of 15 Jan 2024
text: We are a small chocolate maker in the US. We make dark chocolate bars and sell about 500 a week, to shops and online. A 100 g bar sells for $6.20 and costs us about $2.60 to make. Beans come through an importer and take about 4 weeks to arrive; we keep about 6 weeks of stock and could put about $12,000 into more. Our nearest rival, a larger craft brand, sells for $5.90.

search_terms: cocoa futures Ivory Coast Ghana supply

what_happened.text: Cocoa rose above $7,000 a ton in New York for the first time.
Bloomberg reported record cocoa prices hurting chocolate makers such as Nestlé and Hershey.
Cocoa hit an all-time high: $12,567 a tonne in London and $11,878 in New York. By the end of April it was 15% lower.
Prices moved sideways, rallied about 9% by mid-May, then eased after rain in Côte d'Ivoire improved the outlook.

caveats: Cocoa's share of this maker's cost is set at 30%. A UK trade analysis puts cocoa at 30–35% of the production cost of a chocolate bar (mass market, about the 2013/14 season; thegrocer.co.uk/analysis-and-features/cocoa-butter-hikes-add-6p-to-a-chocolate-bar/350125.article). A craft maker's labour and packaging share is larger, so this may overstate it. We found no figure for small bean-to-bar makers.

The series is the world cocoa bean price (Pink Sheet, monthly, $/kg). Makers also buy cocoa butter and powder, which moved differently, and many hedge or buy forward through an importer, so they did not pay the spot price.
Each monthly value is treated as the month's mid-point, with straight lines between them. The monthly average peaked at 9.74 $/kg in April; daily highs were higher.
